milestones.name: On the CPU alone, a spring's water runs down a valley, fills a pool to its sill, quickens through a narrows and reaches a lake, and the solved flow is a chart the water map takes
milestones.quality_bar: A steady river a hydraulics text would accept, held to closed forms as SWASHES' reference cases hold a flood code: discharge kept, pools level, a jump where momentum puts it. Nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: `thrum-river-model` takes a bed grid, declared sources, the bodies water may reach and Manning's `n`, and gives the steady depth and current in every cell. On a valley the test makes, with a spring, a pool behind a sill, a narrows and a basin at its foot: discharge through every cross-section is within 1% of the spring's; away from where the stream enters it the pool's level is flat within 3 cm, and it stands between 1.3 and 1.9 critical depths over its sill; the speed in the narrows over the speed above it is at least the ratio of the wet widths less a fifth; a hollow beside the channel, lower than the water and cut off from it by ground, stays dry.
items.ask: Read the test. Are the expected figures worked out there from continuity and the weir relation, without the solver? Would a solver that routes water down the steepest slope and takes its depth from Manning cell by cell fail the pool?

items.statement: In section the solver meets closed forms the tests work out. Water at rest over a rough bed with dry ground stays at rest to 1e-12 m. A steady flow over a bump has its hydraulic jump within two cells of the closed form's place and a mean depth error under 3% of the critical depth at 0.25 m cells, smaller at 0.125 m. Over a bed made for a known depth with friction, a slow flow is within 1% in depth, and a fast one within 8% at 0.25 m cells and under two thirds of that error at 0.125 m. A sheet on a slope of 0.3 whose bed falls three times its depth across a cell stands within 8% of Manning's normal depth.
items.ask: Are the closed forms in the test its own arithmetic (Bernoulli's branches and the jump condition, a bed integrated for a chosen depth, Manning's normal depth), as in part 1 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py`? Would Audusse's reconstruction, 23% over on the steep sheet there, fail it?

items.statement: Depth is never negative and no value is ever not a number, over 200 seeded beds with dry patches, steps and sources. Below a spring, over ground the start leaves dry, the water wets its way down to the mouth. A solve is refused, by name and place, when water reaches its rectangle's edge, when a source has no way down to a declared body, and when a source body's level anywhere in its range lies below the outlet's sill. Each stretch of channel narrower than four cells is reported by place.

The solve keeps an energy account. The head lost cell by cell, times discharge, sums to the discharge times the head between the source and the mouth within 2%. The chart's loss is the power that breaks the surface, as the design defines it: head lost beyond bed friction, and friction's power beyond the chop's cap. In the section of part 2 the loss at the ledge is at least five times the chute's and fifty times the glide's, and the pool's is under 2% of the ledge's. In the valley of M1.1 at least 60% of the head lost beyond friction lies round its rock and below its narrows and ledge, in under 40% of the wet cells. A straight uniform channel has none: under 1% of its friction power.
items.ask: Does the test compute friction's power from Manning's relation itself and compare, or does it read both sides from the solver's own account?

items.statement: A solve stops when the level's rate and the imbalance of discharge between sections are under the profile's tolerances, and reports its steps, cell updates, seconds and residual. One that does not get there inside its step budget is refused by name and writes nothing. It works on wet cells and their neighbours: doubling the rectangle round the same valley changes its cell updates by under 5%. Two solves of one input give the same bytes, on one thread and on eight.

The solve writes each reach as a chart `thrum-water-model` declares: level over the whole footprint, lying under the bed where the water does not reach, current, loss, footprint, ends and join lengths. With a basin at its mouth and a spring at its head, `thrum-water-model` prepares it with no refusal; the map's level and current at every wet cell's centre are the solver's; the waterline is where the level meets the bed; and the row meets the basin's across the mouth with no step, with the basin's stage at both ends of its range.
items.ask: Is the chart declared only through `thrum-water-model`'s public interface, with no change to that crate in this milestone?

items.statement: A river file holds a solve's output and decodes to the same bytes. Its key is a hash of the bed inside the rectangle, the declaration, the profile and the solver's version; changing a bed cell, a discharge, `n` or the version changes the key, and a file whose key does not match is refused by name. The reader is in `thrum-water-model`, which gains no dependency on the solver.

`scripts/river_cost.py` records a solve of the M1.1 valley at 0.25 m cells on this Mac: wet cells, steps, cell updates and seconds, with the commit, the load on the machine and a release build. `check` fails only when the solve cannot be measured or the committed record lacks one of those. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Was the record taken on this milestone's solver, in a release build, and does it say how its cell updates compare with part 5's count?

milestones.name: On the CPU alone, where the ground drops away the stream leaves it as a waterfall: its path, speed and thickness are worked out, and its water lands in the pool below and runs on
milestones.quality_bar: A fall whose every number follows from the flow at its lip and the height it drops, as a hydraulics text gives a free overfall: nothing placed or tuned by hand, and no water made or lost between the lip and the pool.

items.statement: Brinks are found from the bed alone: runs of faces where the ground, followed downhill, drops at least the profile's least fall (0.75 m) at a slope steeper than the profile's steepest chart slope (1.5). On beds the test makes, a 3 m cliff is a brink along its whole lip; a 0.4 m ledge and a slope of 1 are not, and stay in the chart. The brinks are the same at every discharge.

Water leaves a brink freely and enters the solve again where its path lands. The discharge of the reach below a fall is within 1% of the reach above. The last cell above a lip stands between 0.95 and 1.25 of the critical depth where the flow above is slow, and within 10% of the flow's own depth where it is fast; the fall's launch depth is 0.715 of the critical depth in the first case and the flow's own in the second. The river is cut into reaches at its falls, and the cliff's face is in no chart. A path that lands in a declared basin ends there; one that lands on ground gentler than the steepest chart slope starts a reach there.
items.ask: Does the test show a lower dry cell in place of the lip's face failing the lip's depth, as part 4 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py` does?

items.statement: Ruling 1 is built: a chart may declare a brink end, where the ground drops away below its level. `thrum-water-model` prepares such a chart, gives its own row up to the brink with no mix, and names no body on the ground below; the same chart without the end declared is refused as before. A chart below a fall has no source body. Every existing test of `thrum-water-model` passes unchanged.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test brink_end && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Is the change to the map's preparation confined to a declared brink end, so that no chart an existing test or the example declares is prepared differently? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` edited?

items.statement: A fall record gives, for each place along the lip, the water's path with the time it takes, its discharge for each metre of lip and its launch speed, with stable IDs for its segments. The f64 reference in `thrum-water-model` gives at any point of the path the speed, `sqrt(v0^2 + 2 g z)`; the thickness, discharge over speed; the white share, 0 at the lip and 1 at `6 q^0.32` m of path; and the presence, thickness over the tear thickness and at most 1. Clear of the rock the path is the free path within 1% in throw; where the rock stands in its way it follows the rock's face and never passes through the bed.
items.ask: Are the expected paths, speeds and thicknesses the closed forms of part 4 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py`, worked out in the test?

items.statement: For a body below at any level in its stage's range, the plunge is where each path meets that level, and it moves as the level moves. Each segment's births follow the fall's power, `rho g q z` for each metre of lip, split between foam and submerged air by the profile's share. Each segment's impulse a tick is the wave share times its momentum flux into the surface times the sheet's pattern arriving there, with its mean over the pattern's loop removed: over that loop its mean is under 1% of its rms, its rms is the design's figure within 5%, and the same tick gives the same impulse on every run. A path that lands on bare ground gives no births and no impulses.
`thrum-water-model` still builds with no graphics device and no dependency on the solver, and neither crate's new files or tests hold a place, a preset or a water type that belongs to a game.

milestones.name: On the CPU alone, the river answers its source: it runs deeper, wider and faster as its lake rises, rough in its riffles and smooth in its pools, in a calm as in a gale
milestones.quality_bar: A river whose state follows its lake as a rating curve does, and whose roughness follows its bed as a riffle and a pool do in Red Dead Redemption 2: read between solved flows by the same function a GPU and a game are held to.

items.statement: A river with a source body is solved at levels across that body's stage range no more than 0.3 m apart, and a spring-fed one at the discharges declared. Each sample records its gauge level, and the river reports the range of its gauge. Below a basin with a sill the discharge rises with the level at every sample, and between the lowest and highest sample it grows as the head over the sill to a power between 1.3 and 2.

Ruling 2 is built: in `thrum-water-model` a chart's row is the mix, linear in the gauge, of the two samples that bracket it; the gauge is the source body's level where the river has one and the river's stage where it has none; and every chart of a river takes the same gauge. Between samples 0.3 m apart the mixed row is within 1 cm in depth and 25% in speed of a solve at that level. As the gauge moves 1 cm the waterline on a bank of 1 in 10 or steeper moves by at most one cell. A chart with one sample answers to the bit as before, and its stage adds to its level. Every existing test of `thrum-water-model` passes unchanged.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test gauge && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Does the test compare the mixed row with a fresh solve at the level between, as part 3 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py` does, and would a chart left at one sample with its level raised fail it? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` edited?

items.statement: A fall follows the gauge: its record's discharge, launch speed and path are the mix of its samples', so the sheet's thickness and the plunge's power and impulses grow with the river. A lip the lowest sample leaves dry gives no sheet, no births and no impulses there.

The flow's chop is written as two flow gains in each sample. Its rms height is `c d min(S, S_cap)` from the depth and the friction slope: none at rest; in the valley of M1.1 at least 20 times larger in the riffle than in the pool; never more than 0.15 of the depth. It is all in the short band at 0.15 m of depth and all in the long band at 1 m.
items.ask: Does the test work the expected heights out from Manning's relation at the solver's depths and speeds, with its own arithmetic?

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the CPU: `thrum-water-model` holds the two flow bands' spectrum and an f64 evaluator on the cascades' loop, and its surface model adds them at a chart's flow gains through the same sum, depth limit and moments as a cascade. With no wind, the model's surface over a riffle has the chop's rms height within 10%, and over a sea and a basin it is the level. With the bands not named in the profile every answer of the model is what it was to the bit.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test flow_bands && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model

milestones.quality_bar: Running water as in Red Dead Redemption 2: fast shallows that are rough and bright, slow pools that mirror, detail that travels at the water's own speed and faster in the narrows, and foam in streaks from every rock and ledge, with no sliding sheet, pulse or stamped pattern.

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the GPU. With the wind at nothing, the drawn surface over the riffle has the chop's rms height within the bound this milestone first measures and records against `thrum-water-model`; over the pool it is under a tenth of that; on the lake and the sea it is flat. items.statement: The flow bands are carried by the current. Tracked across submitted frames in a calm where the current is 0.5 m/s and 1.5 m/s, the detail's mean speed downstream is within a fifth of the current; in the pool's still corner it does not drift.

Ruling 4 is built for a chart's loss. Foam is born below the ledge, behind the rocks and down the chute, at a rate that follows the chart's loss, and is carried downstream. With the loss births switched off the foam ages out and none is born. The glide and the pool gain no foam but what the current brings. Lowering the gauge to its lowest sample lowers the cover below the ledge. The record gives the cover each station of the valley reaches and the birth constant used.

There is no sheet sliding at one speed, no pulse at the carriage's period, and no look of a small sea.

milestones.quality_bar: A waterfall as in Horizon Forbidden West, without its mist: falling water that speeds up and stretches as it drops, glassy at the lip and white below, a trickle as strands and a flood as a sheet, and a pool that answers it with foam, pale water and rings.

items.statement: Ruling 7's sheet is built. Each fall is drawn along its record's paths from the lip to the level of the body below, and the depth it writes is within the bound this milestone first measures and records against the f64 reference, with the gauge at each end of its range and the pool's stage at each end of its own. The sheet never shows through the rock it falls past. A scene whose profile does not name falls compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before this milestone.

items.statement: The sheet writes the frame contract. Tracked across submitted frames, its streaks at half the fall's height move at the reference's speed there within 15%, and faster at the foot than at the lip. Its motion output is that movement, from unjittered positions. It writes depth where its presence passes one half and reactive coverage where it is white. A pause holds it, and a capture shows it at the capture's time.

Ruling 4 is built for a plunge and ruling 5 for the mean current. With the interaction windows on the plunge pool, foam and submerged air are born along the plunge line and carried downstream, and rings leave it. The power the rings carry, measured in the model and recorded, is under the fall's. With the gauge at a sample that leaves the lip dry there are no births and no rings. Five seconds after a stone is dropped in the pool, the centre of its rings is within 1.5 m of where the pool's own current carries it, in a window that also holds the riffle. Every existing interaction test of `WATERS` passes unchanged.

milestones.name: A visitor raises the lake, sets the stream's flow and takes the day from dawn to night, and the rivers and the waterfall hold up in motion, in shade and from under water, on the Mac and in Chrome
milestones.quality_bar: Rivers and a waterfall that pass in a shipped high-end game: Red Dead Redemption 2's streams and Horizon Forbidden West's falls, stable under reconstruction, lit only by the engine's sky, and of one piece with the lake and the sea they join.

items.statement: The river selection, the stream's flow and the flow bands are typed controls in the example on the Mac and in Chrome, saved in its parameter file. Moving the stream's flow or the lake's level rebuilds nothing and resets no wake or foam.

Under reconstruction the running water, its foam and the fall hold up in motion: no shimmer on the riffle, no ghost behind a streak of foam or a falling strand, no smear as the camera pans, and a clean reset on a cut and on a change of the selection.

items.statement: Ruling 7's shadow is built. On a sheet, on foam and in the surface's Sun lobe, the direct Sun is multiplied by the scene's lent Sun visibility at the surface point: with half a fall in a wall's shadow, the shadowed half's direct Sun is under 2% of the lit half's, and its sky light is unchanged. A scene with no shadows draws as before.
